content: Knowledge without daily practice is like carrying a heavy bundle of sandalwood on a donkey's back: he feels the weight, but knows nothing of the fragrance.
author: Sanskrit Subhashitas
sourceWork: Yatha khara chandan-bhara-vahi (यथा खरश्चन्दनभारवाही) — Panchatantra & Hitopadesha
explanation: A beast of burden loaded down with thousand-dollar logs of precious aromatics trudges through the mud sweating under the crushing mass, completely oblivious to the celestial perfume on its back. Do not become a beast burdened by unapplied books.
practicalInsight: Pick one moral principle you have studied for years and practice it with absolute precision in your next human interaction.
reflectionPrompt: Are you accumulating degrees, books, and quotes while remaining an overburdened beast who never smells the fragrance of lived wisdom?
